## The model

<details markdown="1">
<summary>The same model, as math</summary>

The file states a plain `n.optimize()`, its multi-period class under the `multi_investment_periods` keyword, and its stochastic class, which `n.set_scenarios(...)` sets. Every quantity chosen once the future is known (second-stage) spans the futures dispatch is chosen in (`scenario`). Capacity is chosen once, before the future is known, and paid at its expected cost in each investment `period` its build year and lifetime span. Operation is the expectation over the scenarios' weights, with a share priced at the worst-outcome mean cost (CVaR) only where a risk preference is set. A plain run's data has one scenario, one period, unit weights, no outage and every `active` flag true, so the problem is the standard one. On a security-constrained run, PyPSA copies each branch flow limit once per `outage`, and the outage factors, `active` flags and scenario weights come from data prep.

| $`\mathrm{ext}^{f}`$ | `Link_p_nom_extendable` over $`\mathcal{L}`$ — whether the nominal power is a decision |
| $`\overline{\mathrm{f}}^{\mathrm{nom}}`$ | `Link_p_nom_max` over $`\mathcal{L} \times \Xi`$ — most nominal power an extendable link may be built at |
| $`\underline{\mathrm{f}}^{\mathrm{nom}}`$ | `Link_p_nom_min` over $`\mathcal{L} \times \Xi`$ — least nominal power an extendable link may be built at |
| $`\mathrm{f}^{\mathrm{mod}}`$ | `Link_p_nom_mod` over $`\mathcal{L}`$, `absent` where the data has no row — the module size a build comes in whole numbers of. No value means the build is continuous |
| $`\mathrm{c}^{f,\mathrm{dn}}`$ | `Link_shut_down_cost` over $`\mathcal{L} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ — cost of one stop in this snapshot |
| $`\mathrm{c}^{f,\mathrm{on}}`$ | `Link_stand_by_cost` over $`\mathcal{L} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ — cost of one snapshot spent on |
| $`\mathrm{c}^{f,\mathrm{up}}`$ | `Link_start_up_cost` over $`\mathcal{L} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ — cost of one start in this snapshot |
| $`\mathrm{u}^{f,0}`$ | `Link_status_initial` over $`\mathcal{L} \times \Xi`$ — one where the link was on before the first snapshot, zero where off. It is PyPSA's `up_time_before > 0` for a committable link, and one for a link that is not, whose ramp rows PyPSA starts from on (`constraints.py:323`), data prep. Under a rolling horizon, it is the status the previous window solved, a fraction where unit commitment is linearised |
| $`\mathrm{on}^{\mathrm{load}}`$ | `Load_active` over $`\mathcal{D}`$ — whether a load is active in the network, PyPSA's `active`. A load has no build year and no lifetime, so the flag is the same in every snapshot. PyPSA refuses one that differs by scenario (`constants.py:54`) |
| $`\mathrm{load}`$ | `Load_p_set` over $`\mathcal{D} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ — demand |
| $`\mathrm{sgn}^{\mathrm{load}}`$ | `Load_sign` over $`\mathcal{D}`$ — the sign a load's demand enters its bus's balance with. It is PyPSA's `sign`, `-1` unless given, `1` for a load that feeds its bus. PyPSA refuses one that differs by scenario (`constants.py:46`) |
| $`\mathrm{on}^{z}`$ | `Process_active` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \mathcal{T}`$ — whether a process is active in a snapshot's period. It is PyPSA's `active`, data prep |

A unit that is active in no snapshot of the horizon still counts. PyPSA refuses one that differs by scenario (`constants.py:54`) |
| $`\mathrm{M}^{z}`$ | `Process_big_m` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi`$, `absent` where the data has no row — the bound a committed extendable process's big-M rows release it by, data prep. It is the build cap `p_nom_max` times the highest `p_max_pu`, where the cap is finite and positive. Elsewhere it is `committable_big_m` times the highest `p_max_pu` (`components.py:1082-1152`). Without that keyword, it is ten times the largest of the peak total load and the component's largest finite `p_nom` and `p_nom_max`. Where there is none of them, it is 1e6. Below the internal power a solve wants, it caps that internal power |
| $`\mathrm{c}^{\mathrm{cap},z}`$ | `Process_capital_cost` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi`$ — cost of one unit of nominal power for the modelled horizon (PyPSA's `periodized_cost`), data prep. It is `overnight_cost` as an annuity over `lifetime` at `discount_rate`, times `nyears`, where `overnight_cost` is given, and `capital_cost` where it is not. Both add `fom_cost` (`components.py:1157-1178`, `costs.py:102-203`) |
| $`\mathrm{W}^{z}`$ | `Process_capital_weight` over $`\mathcal{J}`$ — the sum of period weights a process is active in. It is PyPSA's `active * period_weighting`, summed, data prep |

| $`\mathrm{mnt}^{z}`$ | `Process_maintainable` over $`\mathcal{J}`$ — whether a process must be taken off for maintenance within the horizon: in any scenario, as PyPSA takes the union over them (`components.py:1000-1003`) |

The snapshots it would cover there run past the end of the horizon or into one the process is not active in. It is PyPSA's `active & ~valid`, from `maintenance_duration` and the generator weightings |
| $`\mathrm{c}^{z}`$ | `Process_marginal_cost` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ — cost of one unit of internal power |
| $`\mathrm{c}^{z,(2)}`$ | `Process_marginal_cost_quadratic` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ — cost of the square of one unit of internal power |

Where it does not, the energy still in transit at each period's first snapshots is lost. The flag is the same in every scenario, as the delay is |
| $`\mathrm{d}^{z}`$ | `Process_output_delay` over $`\mathcal{R}`$ — snapshots a port's transfer lags its process's internal power (PyPSA's `delay0`, `delay1`, … read long). In data prep you divide it by the `snapshot_weightings.generators` value and round it up. It is zero for a port that transfers at once. A port has the same delay in every scenario, as a link's port has |

| $`\underline{\mathrm{z}}`$ | `Process_p_min_pu` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ — least internal power, per unit of nominal power: negative for a process that runs both ways |
| $`\mathrm{nonneg}^{z}`$ | `Process_p_min_pu_nonneg` over $`\mathcal{J}`$ — true where none of the process's own minimums-per-unit is negative. It is PyPSA's per-unit `(p_min_pu >= 0).all()` over every snapshot and scenario, data prep |
| $`\mathrm{z}^{\mathrm{nom}}`$ | `Process_p_nom` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi`$ — nominal internal power |
| $`\mathrm{ext}^{z}`$ | `Process_p_nom_extendable` over $`\mathcal{J}`$ — whether the nominal internal power is a decision |
| $`\overline{\mathrm{z}}^{\mathrm{nom}}`$ | `Process_p_nom_max` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi`$ — most nominal power an extendable process may be built at |
| $`\underline{\mathrm{z}}^{\mathrm{nom}}`$ | `Process_p_nom_min` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi`$ — least nominal power an extendable process may be built at |
| $`\mathrm{z}^{\mathrm{mod}}`$ | `Process_p_nom_mod` over $`\mathcal{J}`$, `absent` where the data has no row — the module size a build comes in whole numbers of. No value means the build is continuous |
| $`\alpha`$ | `Process_rate` over $`\mathcal{R} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ — the energy a port draws or delivers per unit of internal power (PyPSA's `rate0`, `rate1`, … read long). It is negative where the port withdraws and positive where it injects. A link is a process whose `bus0` rate is minus one and whose output rates are its efficiencies. The rate at the snapshot the transfer arrives applies, so a delayed port transfers at its arrival snapshot's rate (`constraints.py:1575`) |
| $`\mathrm{c}^{z,\mathrm{dn}}`$ | `Process_shut_down_cost` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ — cost of one stop in this snapshot |

| $`\mathrm{c}^{z,\mathrm{up}}`$ | `Process_start_up_cost` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ — cost of one start in this snapshot |
| $`\mathrm{u}^{z,0}`$ | `Process_status_initial` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi`$ — one where the process was on before the first snapshot, zero where off. It is PyPSA's `up_time_before > 0` for a committable process, and one for a process that is not, whose ramp rows PyPSA starts from on (`constraints.py:323`), data prep. Under a rolling horizon, it is the status the previous window solved, a fraction where unit commitment is linearised |
| $`\mathrm{w}^{y}`$ | `period_weight_objective` over $`\mathcal{Y}`$ — PyPSA's `investment_period_weightings.objective` — what a period's cost weighs. PyPSA reads it only under `multi_investment_periods`. Otherwise you feed one in data prep, whatever the column contains (`optimize.py:231-233`, `:293-297`) |

Where the port is `cyclic_delay`, the delayed flow wraps from the period's end. Where it is not, the flow still in transit at the period's first snapshots is lost. A port that does not delay (`delay` zero) delivers its flow unshifted, cyclic or not |

It is off at the first snapshot it is active in past the first of the horizon. PyPSA reads a status it did not build as off there (`constraints.py:391`). It is the state carried over otherwise |
| $`\mathit{Link\_status\_carried\_over}`$ | `Link_status_carried_over` over $`\mathcal{L} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ — the state a link carries over into a snapshot: the state it brought into the horizon at the first, the previous snapshot's after that |

| $`\mathit{Process\_commitment\_opex}`$ | `Process_commitment_opex` over $`\Xi`$ |
| $`\mathit{Process\_injection}`$ | `Process_injection` over $`\mathcal{N} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ |
| $`\mathrm{Process\_maintenance\_modules}`$ | `Process_maintenance_modules` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi`$ — how many modules of a modular committable process can be on in maintenance: its build cap in modules where the build is extendable, and the modules installed where it is fixed (`constraints.py:588-594`) |
| $`\mathit{Process\_opex}`$ | `Process_opex` over $`\Xi`$ |

Where the port is `cyclic_delay`, the delayed transfer wraps from the period's end. Where it is not, the energy still in transit at the period's first snapshots is lost. A port that does not delay (`delay` zero) transfers at once, cyclic or not |
| $`\mathit{Process\_previous\_status}`$ | `Process_previous_status` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ — the commitment state a process carries into a snapshot. It is off at the first snapshot it is active in past the first of the horizon. PyPSA reads a status it did not build as off there (`constraints.py:391`). It is the state carried over otherwise |
| $`\mathit{Process\_status\_carried\_over}`$ | `Process_status_carried_over` over $`\mathcal{J} \times \Xi \times \mathcal{T}`$ — the state a process carries over into a snapshot: the state it brought into the horizon at the first, the previous snapshot's after that |
| $`\mathit{risk\_weighted\_opex}`$ | `risk_weighted_opex` (scalar) |
| $`\mathit{scenario\_opex}`$ | `scenario_opex` over $`\Xi`$ — what a future costs to run: every operating term, weighted by the snapshot's hours and its period, before the scenario's own weight. A start and a stop cost what they cost, unweighted, as PyPSA adds them (`optimize.py:448-468`) |
| $`\mathit{total\_cost}`$ | `total_cost` (scalar) — what the system costs. Capacity counts once per active period at its expected cost over the scenarios. Operation counts in expectation over the scenarios, and a share of it at the tail |

#### Notation

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $`t \ominus k`$ | `edge='wrap'` — $`t-k`$, cyclic |
| $`t \boxminus_{v} k`$ | `edge=v` — $`t-k`$, and $`v`$ past the edge |
| $`t \ominus^{\mathrm{relation}(t)} k`$ | `within=relation[...]` — $`t-k`$ inside the group of $`t`$ |
| $`\mathrm{pos}(t)`$ | `position()` — the position of $`t`$, counted from $`0`$; $`t`$ is the label |

#### Conditions

**`Generator_com_ext`**

```math
\mathrm{Generator\_com\_ext}_{g,t} \iff \mathrm{com}_{g} \wedge \mathrm{ext}_{g} \wedge \neg \left( \mathrm{p}^{\mathrm{mod}}_{g} > 0 \right) \wedge \mathrm{on}_{g,t} \qquad \forall\, g \in \mathcal{G},\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Generator_committed`**

```math
\mathrm{Generator\_committed}_{g,t} \iff \mathrm{com}_{g} \wedge \mathrm{on}_{g,t} \qquad \forall\, g \in \mathcal{G},\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Generator_maint_ext`**

```math
\mathrm{Generator\_maint\_ext}_{g,t} \iff \mathrm{mnt}_{g} \wedge \mathrm{ext}_{g} \wedge \neg \left( \mathrm{com}_{g} \wedge \mathrm{p}^{\mathrm{mod}}_{g} > 0 \right) \wedge \mathrm{on}_{g,t} \qquad \forall\, g \in \mathcal{G},\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Generator_marginal_cost_curve`**

```math
\mathrm{Generator\_marginal\_cost\_curve}_{g} \iff \lvert \{ b \in \mathcal{B} \,:\, \mathrm{p}^{\mathrm{curve}}_{b,g} \text{ is defined} \} \rvert > 0 \wedge \mathrm{act}_{g} \qquad \forall\, g \in \mathcal{G}
```

**`Link_com_ext`**

```math
\mathrm{Link\_com\_ext}_{l,t} \iff \mathrm{com}^{f}_{l} \wedge \mathrm{ext}^{f}_{l} \wedge \neg \left( \mathrm{f}^{\mathrm{mod}}_{l} > 0 \right) \wedge \mathrm{on}^{f}_{l,t} \qquad \forall\, l \in \mathcal{L},\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Link_committed`**

```math
\mathrm{Link\_committed}_{l,t} \iff \mathrm{com}^{f}_{l} \wedge \mathrm{on}^{f}_{l,t} \qquad \forall\, l \in \mathcal{L},\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Link_maint_ext`**

```math
\mathrm{Link\_maint\_ext}_{l,t} \iff \mathrm{mnt}^{f}_{l} \wedge \mathrm{ext}^{f}_{l} \wedge \neg \left( \mathrm{com}^{f}_{l} \wedge \mathrm{f}^{\mathrm{mod}}_{l} > 0 \right) \wedge \mathrm{on}^{f}_{l,t} \qquad \forall\, l \in \mathcal{L},\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Process_com_ext`**

```math
\mathrm{Process\_com\_ext}_{j,t} \iff \mathrm{com}^{z}_{j} \wedge \mathrm{ext}^{z}_{j} \wedge \neg \left( \mathrm{z}^{\mathrm{mod}}_{j} > 0 \right) \wedge \mathrm{on}^{z}_{j,t} \qquad \forall\, j \in \mathcal{J},\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Process_committed`**

```math
\mathrm{Process\_committed}_{j,t} \iff \mathrm{com}^{z}_{j} \wedge \mathrm{on}^{z}_{j,t} \qquad \forall\, j \in \mathcal{J},\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Process_maint_ext`**

```math
\mathrm{Process\_maint\_ext}_{j,t} \iff \mathrm{mnt}^{z}_{j} \wedge \mathrm{ext}^{z}_{j} \wedge \neg \left( \mathrm{com}^{z}_{j} \wedge \mathrm{z}^{\mathrm{mod}}_{j} > 0 \right) \wedge \mathrm{on}^{z}_{j,t} \qquad \forall\, j \in \mathcal{J},\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

#### Definitions

**`Bus_injection`**

```math
\mathit{Bus\_injection}_{n,\xi,t} = \mathit{Generator\_injection}_{n,\xi,t} + \mathit{Link\_injection}_{n,\xi,t} + \mathrm{Load\_injection}_{n,\xi,t} + \mathit{Process\_injection}_{n,\xi,t} \qquad \forall\, n \in \mathcal{N},\ \xi \in \Xi,\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Generator_capex`**

```math
\mathit{Generator\_capex} = \sum_{g \in \mathcal{G},\ \xi \in \Xi} \pi_{\xi} \cdot P_{g} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{\mathrm{cap}}_{g,\xi} \cdot \mathrm{W}_{g}
```

**`Generator_commitment_opex`**

```math
\mathit{Generator\_commitment\_opex}_{\xi} = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{g \in \mathcal{G}} u_{g,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{\mathrm{on}}_{g,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}_{t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} + \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{g \in \mathcal{G}} \mathit{up}_{g,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{\mathrm{up}}_{g,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} + \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{g \in \mathcal{G}} \mathit{dn}_{g,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{\mathrm{dn}}_{g,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} \qquad \forall\, \xi \in \Xi
```

**`Generator_injection`**

```math
\mathit{Generator\_injection}_{n,\xi,t} = \sum_{g \in \mathcal{G} \,:\, \mathrm{Generator\_bus}(g) = n} \mathrm{sgn}_{g} \cdot p_{g,\xi,t} \qquad \forall\, n \in \mathcal{N},\ \xi \in \Xi,\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Generator_maintenance_modules`**

```math
\mathrm{Generator\_maintenance\_modules}_{g,\xi} = \begin{cases} \frac{\overline{\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{nom}}_{g,\xi}}{\mathrm{p}^{\mathrm{mod}}_{g}} & \text{if } \mathrm{ext}_{g} \\ \mathrm{N}^{\mathrm{fix}}_{g,\xi} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad \forall\, g \in \mathcal{G},\ \xi \in \Xi
```

**`Generator_opex`**

```math
\mathit{Generator\_opex}_{\xi} = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{g \in \mathcal{G}} \mathit{Generator\_running\_cost}_{g,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}_{t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} + \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{g \in \mathcal{G}} p_{g,\xi,t} \cdot p_{g,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{(2)}_{g,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}_{t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} \qquad \forall\, \xi \in \Xi
```

**`Generator_previous_status`**

```math
\mathit{Generator\_previous\_status}_{g,\xi,t} = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } \mathrm{pos}(t) > 0 \wedge \neg \mathrm{on}_{g,t - 1} \\ \mathit{Generator\_status\_carried\_over}_{g,\xi,t} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad \forall\, g \in \mathcal{G},\ \xi \in \Xi,\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Generator_running_cost`**

```math
\mathit{Generator\_running\_cost}_{g,\xi,t} = \begin{cases} C^{\mathrm{curve}}_{g,\xi,t} & \text{if } \mathrm{Generator\_marginal\_cost\_curve}_{g} \\ p_{g,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}_{g,\xi,t} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad \forall\, g \in \mathcal{G},\ \xi \in \Xi,\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Generator_status_carried_over`**

```math
\mathit{Generator\_status\_carried\_over}_{g,\xi,t} = \begin{cases} \mathrm{u}^{0}_{g,\xi} & \text{if } \mathrm{pos}(t) = 0 \\ u_{g,\xi,t - 1} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad \forall\, g \in \mathcal{G},\ \xi \in \Xi,\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Link_capex`**

```math
\mathit{Link\_capex} = \sum_{l \in \mathcal{L},\ \xi \in \Xi} \pi_{\xi} \cdot F_{l} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{\mathrm{cap},f}_{l,\xi} \cdot \mathrm{W}^{f}_{l}
```

**`Link_commitment_opex`**

```math
\mathit{Link\_commitment\_opex}_{\xi} = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{l \in \mathcal{L}} u^{f}_{l,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{f,\mathrm{on}}_{l,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}_{t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} + \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{l \in \mathcal{L}} \mathit{up}^{f}_{l,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{f,\mathrm{up}}_{l,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} + \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{l \in \mathcal{L}} \mathit{dn}^{f}_{l,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{f,\mathrm{dn}}_{l,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} \qquad \forall\, \xi \in \Xi
```

**`Link_injection`**

```math
\mathit{Link\_injection}_{n,\xi,t} = -\left( \sum_{l \in \mathcal{L} \,:\, \mathrm{Link\_bus0}(l) = n} f_{l,\xi,t} \right) + \sum_{o \in \mathcal{O} \,:\, \mathrm{Link\_output\_bus}(o) = n} \mathit{Link\_output\_arrival}_{o,\xi,t} \qquad \forall\, n \in \mathcal{N},\ \xi \in \Xi,\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Link_maintenance_modules`**

```math
\mathrm{Link\_maintenance\_modules}_{l,\xi} = \begin{cases} \frac{\overline{\mathrm{f}}^{\mathrm{nom}}_{l,\xi}}{\mathrm{f}^{\mathrm{mod}}_{l}} & \text{if } \mathrm{ext}^{f}_{l} \\ \mathrm{N}^{f,\mathrm{fix}}_{l,\xi} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad \forall\, l \in \mathcal{L},\ \xi \in \Xi
```

**`Link_opex`**

```math
\mathit{Link\_opex}_{\xi} = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{l \in \mathcal{L}} f_{l,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{f}_{l,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}_{t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} + \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{l \in \mathcal{L}} f_{l,\xi,t} \cdot f_{l,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{f,(2)}_{l,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}_{t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} \qquad \forall\, \xi \in \Xi
```

**`Link_output_arrival`**

```math
\mathit{Link\_output\_arrival}_{o,\xi,t} = \begin{cases} f_{\mathrm{Link\_output\_link}(o),\xi,t \ominus^{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} \mathrm{d}^{f}} \cdot \eta_{o,\xi,t} & \text{if } \mathrm{cyc}^{f}_{o} \\ f_{\mathrm{Link\_output\_link}(o),\xi,t \boxminus_{0}^{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} \mathrm{d}^{f}} \cdot \eta_{o,\xi,t} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad \forall\, o \in \mathcal{O},\ \xi \in \Xi,\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Link_previous_status`**

```math
\mathit{Link\_previous\_status}_{l,\xi,t} = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } \mathrm{pos}(t) > 0 \wedge \neg \mathrm{on}^{f}_{l,t - 1} \\ \mathit{Link\_status\_carried\_over}_{l,\xi,t} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad \forall\, l \in \mathcal{L},\ \xi \in \Xi,\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Link_status_carried_over`**

```math
\mathit{Link\_status\_carried\_over}_{l,\xi,t} = \begin{cases} \mathrm{u}^{f,0}_{l,\xi} & \text{if } \mathrm{pos}(t) = 0 \\ u^{f}_{l,\xi,t - 1} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad \forall\, l \in \mathcal{L},\ \xi \in \Xi,\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Load_demand`**

```math
\mathrm{Load\_demand}_{d,\xi,t} = \begin{cases} \mathrm{sgn}^{\mathrm{load}}_{d} \cdot \mathrm{load}_{d,\xi,t} & \text{if } \mathrm{on}^{\mathrm{load}}_{d} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad \forall\, d \in \mathcal{D},\ \xi \in \Xi,\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Load_injection`**

```math
\mathrm{Load\_injection}_{n,\xi,t} = \sum_{d \in \mathcal{D} \,:\, \mathrm{Load\_bus}(d) = n} \mathrm{Load\_demand}_{d,\xi,t} \qquad \forall\, n \in \mathcal{N},\ \xi \in \Xi,\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Process_capex`**

```math
\mathit{Process\_capex} = \sum_{j \in \mathcal{J},\ \xi \in \Xi} \pi_{\xi} \cdot Z_{j} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{\mathrm{cap},z}_{j,\xi} \cdot \mathrm{W}^{z}_{j}
```

**`Process_commitment_opex`**

```math
\mathit{Process\_commitment\_opex}_{\xi} = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{J}} u^{z}_{j,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{z,\mathrm{on}}_{j,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}_{t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} + \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{J}} \mathit{up}^{z}_{j,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{z,\mathrm{up}}_{j,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} + \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{J}} \mathit{dn}^{z}_{j,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{z,\mathrm{dn}}_{j,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} \qquad \forall\, \xi \in \Xi
```

**`Process_injection`**

```math
\mathit{Process\_injection}_{n,\xi,t} = \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R} \,:\, \mathrm{Process\_output\_bus}(r) = n} \mathit{Process\_output\_arrival}_{r,\xi,t} \qquad \forall\, n \in \mathcal{N},\ \xi \in \Xi,\ t \in \mathcal{T}
```

**`Process_maintenance_modules`**

```math
\mathrm{Process\_maintenance\_modules}_{j,\xi} = \begin{cases} \frac{\overline{\mathrm{z}}^{\mathrm{nom}}_{j,\xi}}{\mathrm{z}^{\mathrm{mod}}_{j}} & \text{if } \mathrm{ext}^{z}_{j} \\ \mathrm{N}^{z,\mathrm{fix}}_{j,\xi} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad \forall\, j \in \mathcal{J},\ \xi \in \Xi
```

**`Process_opex`**

```math
\mathit{Process\_opex}_{\xi} = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{J}} z_{j,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{z}_{j,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}_{t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} + \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{J}} z_{j,\xi,t} \cdot z_{j,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{c}^{z,(2)}_{j,\xi,t} \cdot \mathrm{w}_{t} \cdot \mathrm{w}^{y}_{\mathrm{snapshot\_period}(t)} \qquad \forall\, \xi \in \Xi
```

**`Process_output_arrival`**

```math

```

```math

```

**`Process_status_carried_over`**

```math

```

**`risk_weighted_opex`**

```math
\mathit{risk\_weighted\_opex} = \sum_{\xi \in \Xi} \pi_{\xi} \cdot \mathit{scenario\_opex}_{\xi}
```

**`scenario_opex`**

```math
\mathit{scenario\_opex}_{\xi} = \mathit{Generator\_opex}_{\xi} + \mathit{Generator\_commitment\_opex}_{\xi} + \mathit{Link\_opex}_{\xi} + \mathit{Link\_commitment\_opex}_{\xi} + \mathit{Process\_opex}_{\xi} + \mathit{Process\_commitment\_opex}_{\xi} \qquad \forall\, \xi \in \Xi
```

**`total_cost`**

```math
\mathit{total\_cost} = \mathit{Generator\_capex} + \mathit{Link\_capex} + \mathit{Process\_capex} + \mathit{risk\_weighted\_opex}
```

#### Objective

```math
\min \mathit{total\_cost}
```

    version: 0
    description: The file states a plain `n.optimize()`, its multi-period class under the `multi_investment_periods`
      keyword, and its stochastic class, which `n.set_scenarios(...)` sets. Every quantity chosen once the
      future is known (second-stage) spans the futures dispatch is chosen in (`scenario`). Capacity is chosen
      once, before the future is known, and paid at its expected cost in each investment `period` its build
      year and lifetime span. Operation is the expectation over the scenarios' weights, with a share priced
      at the worst-outcome mean cost (CVaR) only where a risk preference is set. A plain run's data has one
      scenario, one period, unit weights, no outage and every `active` flag true, so the problem is the standard
      one. On a security-constrained run, PyPSA copies each branch flow limit once per `outage`, and the outage
      factors, `active` flags and scenario weights come from data prep.

      breakpoint: {dtype: int, ordered: true, description: 'the corners of a piecewise-linear curve, in order.
          A curve runs over the breakpoints its data has rows for, so curves may differ in length'}
      bus: {description: network nodes}
      generator: {description: 'generating units, each on one bus'}
      link: {description: 'controllable connections, each from one bus to the buses it delivers to'}
      link_output: {description: 'a link''s output ports, one label per port a link declares. The labels are
          PyPSA''s `bus1`, `bus2`, … columns read long, data prep. A link of any number of output ports is
          then one term in the balance'}
      load: {description: 'demands, each on one bus'}
      period: {dtype: int, ordered: true, description: investment periods. It is PyPSA's `investment_periods`}
      process: {description: 'generalised multi-port converters, each with an internal power that every port
          draws or delivers at its own rate'}
      process_output: {description: 'a process''s ports, one label per port a process declares. The labels
          are PyPSA''s `bus0`, `bus1`, …, each with a signed `rate`, data prep. A process of any number of
          ports is then one term in the balance'}
      scenario: {description: 'the futures dispatch is chosen in, each with a weight'}

        description: true where none of the generator's own minimums-per-unit is negative. It is PyPSA's per-unit
          `(p_min_pu >= 0).all()` over every snapshot and scenario, data prep
      Generator_p_nom:
        dims: [generator, scenario]
        description: nominal power
      Generator_p_nom_extendable:
        dims: [generator]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether the nominal power is a decision
      Generator_p_nom_max:
        dims: [generator, scenario]
        description: most nominal power an extendable generator may be built at
      Generator_p_nom_min:
        dims: [generator, scenario]
        description: least nominal power an extendable generator may be built at
      Generator_p_nom_mod:
        dims: [generator]
        missing: absent
        description: the module size a build comes in whole numbers of. No value means the build is continuous
      Generator_shut_down_cost:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one stop in this snapshot
      Generator_sign:
        dims: [generator]
        description: the sign output enters its bus's balance with. It is PyPSA's `sign`, `1` unless given,
          `-1` for a unit that draws power. PyPSA refuses one that differs by scenario (`constants.py:46`)
      Generator_stand_by_cost:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one snapshot spent on
      Generator_start_up_cost:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one start in this snapshot
      Generator_status_initial:
        dims: [generator, scenario]
        description: one where the unit was on before the first snapshot, zero where off. It is PyPSA's `up_time_before
          > 0` for a committable unit, and one for a unit that is not, whose ramp rows PyPSA starts from on
          (`constraints.py:323`), data prep. Under a rolling horizon, it is the status the previous window
          solved, a fraction where unit commitment is linearised
      Link_active:
        dims: [link, snapshot]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a link is active in a snapshot's period. It is PyPSA's `active`, data prep
      Link_active_asset:
        dims: [link]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a link is one of PyPSA's `active_assets`, by its `active` flag alone, without
          build year and lifetime. A unit that is active in no snapshot of the horizon still counts. PyPSA
          refuses one that differs by scenario (`constants.py:54`)
      Link_big_m:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        missing: absent
        description: the bound a committed extendable link's big-M rows release it by, data prep. It is the
          build cap `p_nom_max` times the highest `p_max_pu`, where the cap is finite and positive. Elsewhere
          it is `committable_big_m` times the highest `p_max_pu` (`components.py:1082-1152`). Without that
          keyword, it is ten times the largest of the peak total load and the component's largest finite `p_nom`
          and `p_nom_max`. Where there is none of them, it is 1e6. Below the flow a solve wants, it caps that
          flow
      Link_capital_cost:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: cost of one unit of nominal power for the modelled horizon (PyPSA's `periodized_cost`),
          data prep. It is `overnight_cost` as an annuity over `lifetime` at `discount_rate`, times `nyears`,
          where `overnight_cost` is given, and `capital_cost` where it is not. Both add `fom_cost` (`components.py:1157-1178`,
          `costs.py:102-203`)
      Link_capital_weight:
        dims: [link]
        description: the sum of period weights a link is active in. It is PyPSA's `active * period_weighting`,
          summed, data prep
      Link_committable:
        dims: [link]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether flow is gated by an on/off status decision
      Link_efficiency:
        dims: [link_output, scenario, snapshot]
        description: 'share of the flow that arrives at an output port, PyPSA''s `efficiency`, `efficiency2`,
          … read long: negative where that port consumes rather than delivers. Read at the snapshot the flow
          arrives, so a delayed port delivers at its arrival snapshot''s efficiency (`constraints.py:1575`)'
      Link_maintainable:
        dims: [link]
        dtype: bool
        description: 'whether a link must be taken off for maintenance within the horizon: in any scenario,
          as PyPSA takes the union over them (`components.py:1000-1003`)'
      Link_maintenance_events:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        dtype: int
        description: how many maintenance events occur within the horizon
      Link_maintenance_pu:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: the share of the build a maintenance event takes off
      Link_maintenance_start_blocked:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        dtype: bool
        description: true where no maintenance event may start, data prep. The snapshots it would cover there
          run past the end of the horizon or into one the link is not active in. It is PyPSA's `active & ~valid`,
          from `maintenance_duration` and the generator weightings
      Link_marginal_cost:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one unit of flow
      Link_marginal_cost_quadratic:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of the square of one unit of flow
      Link_modules_installed:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: how many whole modules a committable build has in place, data prep. It is `Link_p_nom
          / Link_p_nom_mod` where a fixed build is modular, and one where it is not. PyPSA refuses a fixed
          modular build whose nominal power is not a whole number of modules
      Link_output_cyclic_delay:
        dims: [link_output]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a delayed port's flow wraps from the end of its investment period (PyPSA's `cyclic_delay`,
          `cyclic_delay2`, …). Where it does not, the flow still in transit at each period's first snapshots
          is lost. The flag is the same in every scenario, as the delay is
      Link_output_delay:
        dims: [link_output]
        dtype: int
        description: snapshots a port's delivery lags its link's flow (PyPSA's `delay`, `delay2`, … read long).
          In data prep you divide it by the `snapshot_weightings.generators` value and round it up. It is
          zero for a port that delivers at once. A port has the same delay in every scenario, because PyPSA
          refuses a delay that differs by scenario (`constants.py:55`)
      Link_p_max_pu:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: most flow, per unit of nominal power
      Link_p_min_pu:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: 'least flow, per unit of nominal power: negative for a link that carries both ways'
      Link_p_min_pu_nonneg:
        dims: [link]
        dtype: bool
        description: true where none of the link's own minimums-per-unit is negative. It is PyPSA's per-unit
          `(p_min_pu >= 0).all()` over every snapshot and scenario, data prep
      Link_p_nom:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: nominal power
      Link_p_nom_extendable:
        dims: [link]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether the nominal power is a decision
      Link_p_nom_max:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: most nominal power an extendable link may be built at
      Link_p_nom_min:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: least nominal power an extendable link may be built at
      Link_p_nom_mod:
        dims: [link]
        missing: absent
        description: the module size a build comes in whole numbers of. No value means the build is continuous
      Link_shut_down_cost:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one stop in this snapshot
      Link_stand_by_cost:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one snapshot spent on
      Link_start_up_cost:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one start in this snapshot
      Link_status_initial:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: one where the link was on before the first snapshot, zero where off. It is PyPSA's `up_time_before
          > 0` for a committable link, and one for a link that is not, whose ramp rows PyPSA starts from on
          (`constraints.py:323`), data prep. Under a rolling horizon, it is the status the previous window
          solved, a fraction where unit commitment is linearised
      Load_active:
        dims: [load]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a load is active in the network, PyPSA's `active`. A load has no build year and
          no lifetime, so the flag is the same in every snapshot. PyPSA refuses one that differs by scenario
          (`constants.py:54`)
      Load_p_set:
        dims: [load, scenario, snapshot]
        description: demand
      Load_sign:
        dims: [load]
        description: the sign a load's demand enters its bus's balance with. It is PyPSA's `sign`, `-1` unless
          given, `1` for a load that feeds its bus. PyPSA refuses one that differs by scenario (`constants.py:46`)
      Process_active:
        dims: [process, snapshot]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a process is active in a snapshot's period. It is PyPSA's `active`, data prep
      Process_active_asset:
        dims: [process]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a process is one of PyPSA's `active_assets`, by its `active` flag alone, without
          build year and lifetime. A unit that is active in no snapshot of the horizon still counts. PyPSA
          refuses one that differs by scenario (`constants.py:54`)
      Process_big_m:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        missing: absent
        description: the bound a committed extendable process's big-M rows release it by, data prep. It is
          the build cap `p_nom_max` times the highest `p_max_pu`, where the cap is finite and positive. Elsewhere
          it is `committable_big_m` times the highest `p_max_pu` (`components.py:1082-1152`). Without that
          keyword, it is ten times the largest of the peak total load and the component's largest finite `p_nom`
          and `p_nom_max`. Where there is none of them, it is 1e6. Below the internal power a solve wants,
          it caps that internal power
      Process_capital_cost:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: cost of one unit of nominal power for the modelled horizon (PyPSA's `periodized_cost`),
          data prep. It is `overnight_cost` as an annuity over `lifetime` at `discount_rate`, times `nyears`,
          where `overnight_cost` is given, and `capital_cost` where it is not. Both add `fom_cost` (`components.py:1157-1178`,
          `costs.py:102-203`)
      Process_capital_weight:
        dims: [process]
        description: the sum of period weights a process is active in. It is PyPSA's `active * period_weighting`,
          summed, data prep
      Process_committable:
        dims: [process]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether internal power is gated by an on/off status decision
      Process_maintainable:
        dims: [process]
        dtype: bool
        description: 'whether a process must be taken off for maintenance within the horizon: in any scenario,
          as PyPSA takes the union over them (`components.py:1000-1003`)'
      Process_maintenance_events:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        dtype: int
        description: how many maintenance events occur within the horizon
      Process_maintenance_pu:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: the share of the build a maintenance event takes off
      Process_maintenance_start_blocked:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        dtype: bool
        description: true where no maintenance event may start, data prep. The snapshots it would cover there
          run past the end of the horizon or into one the process is not active in. It is PyPSA's `active
          & ~valid`, from `maintenance_duration` and the generator weightings
      Process_marginal_cost:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one unit of internal power
      Process_marginal_cost_quadratic:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of the square of one unit of internal power
      Process_modules_installed:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: how many whole modules a committable build has in place, data prep. It is `Process_p_nom
          / Process_p_nom_mod` where a fixed build is modular, and one where it is not. PyPSA refuses a fixed
          modular build whose nominal power is not a whole number of modules
      Process_output_cyclic_delay:
        dims: [process_output]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a delayed port's transfer wraps from the end of its investment period (PyPSA's
          `cyclic_delay0`, `cyclic_delay1`, …). Where it does not, the energy still in transit at each period's
          first snapshots is lost. The flag is the same in every scenario, as the delay is
      Process_output_delay:
        dims: [process_output]
        dtype: int
        description: snapshots a port's transfer lags its process's internal power (PyPSA's `delay0`, `delay1`,
          … read long). In data prep you divide it by the `snapshot_weightings.generators` value and round
          it up. It is zero for a port that transfers at once. A port has the same delay in every scenario,
          as a link's port has
      Process_p_max_pu:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: most internal power, per unit of nominal power
      Process_p_min_pu:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: 'least internal power, per unit of nominal power: negative for a process that runs both
          ways'
      Process_p_min_pu_nonneg:
        dims: [process]
        dtype: bool
        description: true where none of the process's own minimums-per-unit is negative. It is PyPSA's per-unit
          `(p_min_pu >= 0).all()` over every snapshot and scenario, data prep
      Process_p_nom:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: nominal internal power
      Process_p_nom_extendable:
        dims: [process]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether the nominal internal power is a decision
      Process_p_nom_max:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: most nominal power an extendable process may be built at
      Process_p_nom_min:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: least nominal power an extendable process may be built at
      Process_p_nom_mod:
        dims: [process]
        missing: absent
        description: the module size a build comes in whole numbers of. No value means the build is continuous
      Process_rate:
        dims: [process_output, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the energy a port draws or delivers per unit of internal power (PyPSA's `rate0`, `rate1`,
          … read long). It is negative where the port withdraws and positive where it injects. A link is a
          process whose `bus0` rate is minus one and whose output rates are its efficiencies. The rate at
          the snapshot the transfer arrives applies, so a delayed port transfers at its arrival snapshot's
          rate (`constraints.py:1575`)
      Process_shut_down_cost:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one stop in this snapshot
      Process_stand_by_cost:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one snapshot spent on
      Process_start_up_cost:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one start in this snapshot
      Process_status_initial:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: one where the process was on before the first snapshot, zero where off. It is PyPSA's
          `up_time_before > 0` for a committable process, and one for a process that is not, whose ramp rows
          PyPSA starts from on (`constraints.py:323`), data prep. Under a rolling horizon, it is the status
          the previous window solved, a fraction where unit commitment is linearised
      period_weight_objective:
        dims: [period]
        description: PyPSA's `investment_period_weightings.objective` — what a period's cost weighs. PyPSA
          reads it only under `multi_investment_periods`. Otherwise you feed one in data prep, whatever the
          column contains (`optimize.py:231-233`, `:293-297`)
      scenario_weight:
        dims: [scenario]
        description: PyPSA's `scenario_weightings.weight` — the probability of a future
      snapshot_weightings_objective:
        dims: [snapshot]
        description: PyPSA's `snapshot_weightings.objective` — hours a snapshot weighs in the cost
    variables:
      Generator_maintenance:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_maintainable AND Generator_active
        bounds: {lower: 0.0, upper: 1.0}
        missing: 0.0
        description: '`Generator-maintenance` — whether a maintainable generator is in maintenance: continuous,
          and one exactly where an event covers the snapshot'
      Generator_maintenance_capacity:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_maint_ext
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        missing: 0.0
        description: '`Generator-maintenance_capacity` — the chosen build while in maintenance, zero otherwise:
          the product the `maintcap` rows linearise'
      Generator_maintenance_start:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_maintainable AND Generator_active
        domain: binary
        missing: 0.0
        description: '`Generator-maintenance_start` — whether a maintenance event starts in this snapshot'
      Generator_maintenance_status:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_maintainable AND Generator_committed AND NOT (Generator_p_nom_extendable AND NOT
          (Generator_p_nom_mod > 0))
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        missing: 0.0
        description: '`Generator-maintenance_status` — the status while in maintenance, zero otherwise: the
          product the `maint-status` rows linearise, so a unit in maintenance may also be off'
      Generator_n_mod:
        dims: [generator]
        where: Generator_p_nom_extendable AND Generator_p_nom_mod > 0 AND Generator_active_asset
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Generator-n_mod` — how many modules of an extendable modular build. A unit that is
          not active has none'
      Generator_p:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_active
        description: '`Generator-p` — output of a generator in a snapshot'
      Generator_p_nom_ext:
        dims: [generator]
        where: Generator_p_nom_extendable AND Generator_active_asset
        description: '`Generator-p_nom` — nominal power where it is a decision, for a generator that is active.
          A fixed build is the parameter of the same PyPSA name'
      Generator_shut_down:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Generator-shut_down` — how much of a committable unit turns off this snapshot, capped
          as the status is'
      Generator_start_up:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Generator-start_up` — how much of a committable unit turns on this snapshot, capped
          as the status is'
      Generator_status:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Generator-status` — how much of a committable unit is on. It is an integer the rows
          below cap at one, or at the module count where the build is modular'
      Link_maintenance:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_maintainable AND Link_active
        bounds: {lower: 0.0, upper: 1.0}
        missing: 0.0
        description: '`Link-maintenance` — whether a maintainable link is in maintenance: continuous, and
          one exactly where an event covers the snapshot'
      Link_maintenance_capacity:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_maint_ext
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        missing: 0.0
        description: '`Link-maintenance_capacity` — the chosen build while in maintenance, zero otherwise:
          the product the `maintcap` rows linearise'
      Link_maintenance_start:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_maintainable AND Link_active
        domain: binary
        missing: 0.0
        description: '`Link-maintenance_start` — whether a maintenance event starts in this snapshot'
      Link_maintenance_status:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_maintainable AND Link_committed AND NOT (Link_p_nom_extendable AND NOT (Link_p_nom_mod
          > 0))
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        missing: 0.0
        description: '`Link-maintenance_status` — the status while in maintenance, zero otherwise: the product
          the `maint-status` rows linearise, so a unit in maintenance may also be off'
      Link_n_mod:
        dims: [link]
        where: Link_p_nom_extendable AND Link_p_nom_mod > 0 AND Link_active_asset
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Link-n_mod` — how many modules of an extendable modular build. A unit that is not active
          has none'
      Link_p:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_active
        description: '`Link-p` — PyPSA''s `p0`, the flow measured at the `Link_bus0` end. A positive value
          withdraws there and injects at every bus the link''s output ports deliver to'
      Link_p_nom_ext:
        dims: [link]
        where: Link_p_nom_extendable AND Link_active_asset
        description: '`Link-p_nom` — nominal power where it is a decision, for a link that is active. A fixed
          build is the parameter of the same PyPSA name'
      Link_shut_down:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Link-shut_down` — how much of a committable link turns off this snapshot, capped as
          the status is'
      Link_start_up:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Link-start_up` — how much of a committable link turns on this snapshot, capped as the
          status is'
      Link_status:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Link-status` — how much of a committable link is on. It is an integer the rows below
          cap at one, or at the module count where the build is modular'
      Process_maintenance:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_maintainable AND Process_active
        bounds: {lower: 0.0, upper: 1.0}
        missing: 0.0
        description: '`Process-maintenance` — whether a maintainable process is in maintenance: continuous,
          and one exactly where an event covers the snapshot'
      Process_maintenance_capacity:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_maint_ext
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        missing: 0.0
        description: '`Process-maintenance_capacity` — the chosen build while in maintenance, zero otherwise:
          the product the `maintcap` rows linearise'
      Process_maintenance_start:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_maintainable AND Process_active
        domain: binary
        missing: 0.0
        description: '`Process-maintenance_start` — whether a maintenance event starts in this snapshot'
      Process_maintenance_status:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_maintainable AND Process_committed AND NOT (Process_p_nom_extendable AND NOT (Process_p_nom_mod
          > 0))
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        missing: 0.0
        description: '`Process-maintenance_status` — the status while in maintenance, zero otherwise: the
          product the `maint-status` rows linearise, so a unit in maintenance may also be off'
      Process_n_mod:
        dims: [process]
        where: Process_p_nom_extendable AND Process_p_nom_mod > 0 AND Process_active_asset
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Process-n_mod` — how many modules of an extendable modular build. A unit that is not
          active has none'
      Process_p:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_active
        description: '`Process-p` — PyPSA''s internal power `p`. A positive value drives every port at its
          own rate, withdrawing where the rate is negative and injecting where it is positive'
      Process_p_nom_ext:
        dims: [process]
        where: Process_p_nom_extendable AND Process_active_asset
        description: '`Process-p_nom` — nominal internal power where it is a decision, for a process that
          is active. A fixed build is the parameter of the same PyPSA name'
      Process_shut_down:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Process-shut_down` — how much of a committable process turns off this snapshot, capped
          as the status is'
      Process_start_up:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Process-start_up` — how much of a committable process turns on this snapshot, capped
          as the status is'
      Process_status:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Process-status` — how much of a committable process is on. It is an integer the rows
          below cap at one, or at the module count where the build is modular'
      Generator_marginal_cost_piecewise:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_marginal_cost_curve AND Generator_active
        description: '`Generator-marginal_cost_piecewise` — the running cost of a generator that pays along
          a curve, held above the curve'
    constraints:
      Bus_nodal_balance:
        dims: [bus, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Bus_attached
        expression: Bus_injection == 0
        description: '`Bus-nodal_balance` — what is generated at a bus meets the load there, less half of
          every incident line''s and transformer''s loss. What is generated includes storage dispatch and
          stores. It is net of what the links take away, plus what arrives over them after losses and any
          delay at every port they deliver to. Each process port draws or delivers at its own rate, and each
          passive branch carries its flow. PyPSA dissipates a branch''s loss half at either end. Each generator,
          storage unit, store and load term enters with its component''s `sign` (`constraints.py:1480-1481`,
          `:1592`), and an inactive load not at all. A bus nothing is attached to has no row. PyPSA refuses
          one that carries load. The file states no assumption for it.'
      Generator_com_ext_p_lower:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_com_ext
        expression: Generator_p >= Generator_p_min_pu * (Generator_p_nom_ext - Generator_maintenance_pu *
          Generator_maintenance_capacity) + Generator_big_m * Generator_status - Generator_big_m
        description: '`Generator-com-ext-p-lower` — a committed extendable unit outputs at least its minimum
          of the chosen build. Off, the big M releases the row'
      Generator_com_ext_p_lower_nonneg:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_com_ext AND Generator_p_min_pu_nonneg
        expression: Generator_p >= 0
